stories.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
stories.subtitle: Peace in the middle of fear
stories.description: Join the disciples in a violent storm and see Jesus bring calm to the wind, waves and fearful hearts.

introduction.summary: When a violent storm overwhelms experienced fishermen, Jesus speaks peace to the wind and waves and asks his disciples to consider where their faith is placed.
introduction.context: Jesus has been teaching beside the Sea of Galilee. As evening comes, he asks the disciples to cross to the other side, and they leave while other boats accompany them.

storySections.title: Cross to the Other Side
storySections.content: After a demanding day of teaching, Jesus tells the disciples to cross the lake. They take him in the boat just as he is. The journey begins in obedience to his direction, not because the disciples have chosen an unsafe route on their own.

storySections.title: The Storm Rises
storySections.content: A sudden, powerful storm sweeps across the lake. Waves break over the boat until it begins filling with water. Several disciples understand boats and weather, yet the situation exceeds their ability to control it.

storySections.title: Jesus Is Awakened
storySections.content: Jesus is sleeping on a cushion in the stern. The frightened disciples wake him with an urgent accusation that he does not care whether they die. Their prayer is honest, but fear has distorted how they interpret his presence.

storySections.title: Quiet, Be Still
storySections.content: Jesus rises, rebukes the wind and commands the sea to become still. The wind stops and the water becomes calm. The same authority visible in his teaching is now displayed over the forces of nature.

storySections.title: Who Is This?
storySections.content: Jesus asks why the disciples are afraid and why they still lack faith. Their fear of the storm becomes reverent wonder as they ask who he is, since even wind and waves obey him.

keyPeople.name: Jesus
keyPeople.role: Teacher whose authority extends over the wind and sea

keyPeople.name: The disciples
keyPeople.role: Followers who move from panic toward deeper recognition of Jesus

keyLocations.name: Sea of Galilee
keyLocations.description: Freshwater lake known for sudden storms

keyLocations.name: The boat
keyLocations.description: Setting where danger, honest fear and divine authority meet

flashcards.front: Who suggested crossing the lake?
flashcards.back: Jesus told the disciples to go to the other side.

flashcards.front: What endangered the boat?
flashcards.back: A violent windstorm drove waves into the boat until it began filling.

flashcards.front: Where was Jesus during the storm?
flashcards.back: He was asleep on a cushion in the stern.

flashcards.front: How did the disciples wake Jesus?
flashcards.back: They urgently questioned whether he cared that they were in danger.

flashcards.front: What happened when Jesus spoke?
flashcards.back: The wind stopped and the sea became completely calm.

flashcards.front: What question did the disciples ask afterwards?
flashcards.back: They wondered who Jesus was, because even the wind and sea obeyed him.

keyLessons: Obedience does not guarantee a life without storms.
Fear can make us question God’s care even when he is present.
Honest prayer can bring fear directly to Jesus.
Jesus’ authority is greater than the forces that overwhelm us.
Faith grows by learning who Jesus is, not by denying danger.

reflection.question: What current situation feels beyond your ability to control?
reflection.prompt: Describe the fear honestly, then write one truth about Jesus’ presence or character that can guide your response.

stories.prayerPrompt: Jesus, meet me in what I cannot control and teach me to trust your presence in the storm.

quiz.question: Where were Jesus and the disciples travelling?
quiz.explanation: Jesus asked them to cross the lake to the other side.

quiz.question: What was Jesus doing when the storm intensified?
quiz.explanation: Jesus was asleep on a cushion at the back of the boat.

quiz.question: What did Jesus address first after waking?
quiz.explanation: Jesus rebuked the wind and commanded the sea to be still.

quiz.question: What happened immediately after Jesus spoke?
quiz.explanation: The wind ceased and the lake became calm.

quiz.question: What did the disciples’ final question focus on?
quiz.explanation: The miracle caused them to ask who Jesus truly was.

stories.title: The Good Samaritan
stories.subtitle: Love that crosses every boundary
stories.description: Hear Jesus reveal true neighbourly love through a Samaritan who stops, serves and shows compassion.

introduction.summary: Jesus answers a question about neighbourly love with a story in which the expected outsider becomes the true neighbour through practical compassion.
introduction.context: An expert in the law asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life and then seeks to narrow the command to love one’s neighbour by asking who qualifies as a neighbour.

storySections.title: The Question
storySections.content: A legal expert tests Jesus with a question about eternal life. Jesus directs him to the law, and the man correctly joins love for God with love for one’s neighbour. Wanting to justify himself, he asks Jesus to define the limits of neighbourly responsibility.

storySections.title: The Road to Jericho
storySections.content: Jesus describes a traveller attacked by robbers on the dangerous road from Jerusalem to Jericho. They strip him, beat him and leave him barely alive. The injured man is not given a name, profession or ethnicity that might make compassion easier to calculate.

storySections.title: Passing By
storySections.content: A priest sees the wounded man and passes on the other side. A Levite comes, sees and also passes by. Both are associated with religious service, yet neither turns observation into help.

storySections.title: Compassion in Action
storySections.content: A Samaritan sees the man and is moved with compassion. Despite hostility between their communities, he approaches, treats the wounds, places the man on his own animal and brings him to an inn.

storySections.title: Go and Do Likewise
storySections.content: The Samaritan pays for ongoing care and promises to cover additional costs. Jesus changes the original question: instead of deciding who deserves to be called a neighbour, the listener must become a neighbour to the person in need. The expert identifies the merciful man, and Jesus tells him to act likewise.

keyPeople.name: Jesus
keyPeople.role: Teacher who tells the parable

keyPeople.name: The legal expert
keyPeople.role: Questioner challenged to practise mercy

keyPeople.name: The injured traveller
keyPeople.role: Vulnerable person whose need exposes the character of others

keyPeople.name: The Samaritan
keyPeople.role: Unexpected neighbour who provides compassionate care

keyPeople.name: The priest and Levite
keyPeople.role: Religious figures who see the need but pass by

keyLocations.name: Road from Jerusalem to Jericho
keyLocations.description: Steep, isolated route used as the parable’s setting

keyLocations.name: The inn
keyLocations.description: Place where the Samaritan arranges continuing care

flashcards.front: Why did the legal expert ask who his neighbour was?
flashcards.back: He wanted to justify himself and define the limits of his obligation.

flashcards.front: What happened to the traveller?
flashcards.back: Robbers stripped, beat and abandoned him in a critical condition.

flashcards.front: Which two people passed by?
flashcards.back: A priest and a Levite both saw the man and continued on.

flashcards.front: Who stopped to help?
flashcards.back: A Samaritan traveller was moved with compassion.

flashcards.front: What practical care did the Samaritan provide?
flashcards.back: He treated the wounds, transported the man, found shelter and paid for continuing care.

flashcards.front: How did Jesus redefine being a neighbour?
flashcards.back: A neighbour is someone who chooses to show mercy to the person in need.

keyLessons: Love for God and love for people cannot be separated.
Seeing suffering is not the same as responding compassionately.
Neighbourly love crosses social, ethnic and religious hostility.
Mercy is practical, costly and attentive to ongoing needs.
The better question is not who qualifies for our love, but how we can become loving neighbours.

reflection.question: Whose need might be easy for you to see but inconvenient to engage?
reflection.prompt: Choose one safe, practical act of mercy that respects the person’s dignity and actual needs.

stories.prayerPrompt: Compassionate God, free me from indifference and teach me to become a neighbour through practical mercy.

quiz.question: What second question did the legal expert ask Jesus?
quiz.explanation: The man sought to define whom he was required to love.

quiz.question: Where was the injured man travelling?
quiz.explanation: The parable is set on the road descending from Jerusalem to Jericho.

quiz.question: Who passed by without helping?
quiz.explanation: Both religious figures saw the man but crossed away from him.

quiz.question: What moved the Samaritan to respond?
quiz.explanation: His inward compassion became practical action.

quiz.question: What did Jesus tell the expert to do?
options: Go and practise the same mercy
quiz.explanation: Jesus called him to imitate the Samaritan’s merciful action.

stories.title: The Prodigal Son
stories.subtitle: The Father who welcomes us home
stories.description: Discover a father’s extravagant welcome and the restoring grace offered to both of his sons.

introduction.summary: Jesus tells of a younger son who wastes his inheritance, a father who welcomes him home and an older son who struggles to share the father’s joy.
introduction.context: Religious leaders criticise Jesus for welcoming people they regard as sinners. The parable is the third in a sequence about something lost being found.

storySections.title: A Costly Demand
storySections.content: The younger of two sons asks his father for his share of the estate before the father’s death. The father divides the property. Soon afterwards, the son converts his portion into resources and travels to a distant country.

storySections.title: Everything Lost
storySections.content: The younger son wastes his wealth in reckless living. When a severe famine comes, he has no reserves and becomes desperate. He takes work feeding pigs and longs to eat their food, but no one gives him anything.

storySections.title: Coming to His Senses
storySections.content: Remembering that his father’s hired workers have enough food, the son recognises his sin against heaven and his father. He prepares no excuse. He plans to return, confess and ask to be treated as a worker rather than a son.

storySections.title: The Father Runs
storySections.content: While the son is still far away, the father sees him, is filled with compassion and runs to embrace him. Before the son can finish his prepared request, the father orders a robe, ring and sandals and begins a celebration because the lost son has returned.

storySections.title: The Older Brother
storySections.content: The older son hears the celebration and refuses to enter. He sees his obedience as unpaid labour and resents his brother’s welcome. The father goes out to him too, affirming his place while explaining that the restoration of the lost brother deserves joy.

keyPeople.name: Jesus
keyPeople.role: Teacher who tells the parable in response to criticism

keyPeople.name: The father
keyPeople.role: Figure of generous compassion who goes out to both sons

keyPeople.name: The younger son
keyPeople.role: Lost son who returns in repentance

keyPeople.name: The older son
keyPeople.role: Faithful-looking son whose resentment keeps him outside the celebration

keyLocations.name: The distant country
keyLocations.description: Place of the younger son’s self-directed life and loss

keyLocations.name: The father’s home
keyLocations.description: Place of abundance, restored relationship and celebration

flashcards.front: What did the younger son request?
flashcards.back: He asked for his share of the family estate.

flashcards.front: What happened after he spent everything?
flashcards.back: A severe famine came, and he became desperately poor.

flashcards.front: What marked the son’s turning point?
flashcards.back: He came to his senses, admitted his sin and decided to return home.

flashcards.front: How did the father respond when he saw him?
flashcards.back: The father ran to him with compassion, embraced him and welcomed him.

flashcards.front: What gifts signalled restored sonship?
flashcards.back: The father provided the best robe, a ring and sandals.

flashcards.front: Why did the older brother refuse to celebrate?
flashcards.back: He resented the welcome given to his brother and viewed his own service as unrewarded labour.

keyLessons: Sin promises independence but can lead to isolation and loss.
Repentance faces the truth and turns toward home without excuses.
God’s grace restores relationship beyond what we can earn.
Religious obedience can still hide resentment and self-righteousness.
The Father goes out in compassion to both the openly lost and the resentfully distant.

reflection.question: Do you identify more with the younger son’s wandering or the older son’s resentment?
reflection.prompt: Name what returning to the Father would look like in your present situation.

stories.prayerPrompt: Gracious Father, bring me home from both rebellion and resentment, and teach me to rejoice when others receive mercy.

quiz.question: What did the younger son do after receiving his inheritance?
quiz.explanation: He left home and wasted his resources far away.

quiz.question: What work did the son eventually take?
quiz.explanation: His desperate condition is shown by his work among pigs and his hunger.

quiz.question: What did the son decide to do?
quiz.explanation: He recognised his wrongdoing and set out for his father.

quiz.question: Who first saw the returning son?
quiz.explanation: The father saw him while he was still far away.

quiz.question: Who remained outside the celebration?
quiz.explanation: The older brother refused to enter because he was angry.

stories.title: The Cross
stories.subtitle: Love’s greatest sacrifice
stories.description: Reflect on Jesus’ suffering, forgiveness and self-giving love as he goes willingly to the cross.
stories.contentAdvisory: This story includes betrayal, injustice and a non-graphic account of execution. Younger readers may benefit from reading it with a trusted adult.

introduction.summary: Jesus willingly enters suffering, is unjustly condemned and dies on the cross. The Gospel accounts present the cross as the costly centre of his saving mission and self-giving love.
introduction.context: During Passover week in Jerusalem, opposition to Jesus reaches its climax. His closest followers are confused and afraid, yet Jesus continues to act with purpose, prayer and love.

storySections.title: The Last Supper
storySections.content: Jesus shares the Passover meal with his disciples. He gives bread and the cup new significance, connecting them with his body and the covenant established through his life given for others. He also warns that betrayal is near.

storySections.title: Prayer in the Garden
storySections.content: In Gethsemane, Jesus experiences deep anguish and asks his closest disciples to keep watch. He honestly brings his suffering before the Father while yielding himself to the Father’s will. The disciples struggle to remain awake.

storySections.title: Betrayal and Trial
storySections.content: Judas arrives with an armed group and identifies Jesus. Jesus is arrested, questioned and taken to the Roman governor. Though Pilate recognises problems with the accusations, public pressure and political fear lead him to authorise crucifixion.

storySections.title: The Cross
storySections.content: Jesus is taken outside the city and crucified between two criminals. The Gospel writers describe mockery, darkness and Jesus’ concern for others even while suffering. At his death, the temple curtain is torn, and a Roman centurion recognises that Jesus is righteous and truly God’s Son.

storySections.title: Laid in a Tomb
storySections.content: Joseph of Arimathea asks for Jesus’ body and places it in a new tomb. Women who followed Jesus observe where he is laid and prepare spices, then rest on the Sabbath. Grief and silence close the day, but this is not the end of the story.

flashcards.front: What meal did Jesus share before his arrest?

flashcards.front: Where did Jesus pray in anguish?

flashcards.front: Who betrayed Jesus?

flashcards.front: Which Roman governor authorised the execution?

keyLessons: Jesus brings honest anguish into obedient prayer.
Political convenience and crowd pressure can produce grave injustice.
At the cross, Jesus continues to embody forgiveness and self-giving love.
Christian hope takes suffering and death seriously rather than denying them.
The cross must be understood together with the resurrection that follows.

reflection.question: What does Jesus’ self-giving love reveal about the value God places on reconciliation?
reflection.prompt: Spend time in gratitude, then consider one relationship in which costly forgiveness, truth or reconciliation may be needed.

stories.prayerPrompt: Jesus, thank you for your self-giving love. Form in me humility, courage, forgiveness and faithful hope.

stories.title: The Resurrection
stories.subtitle: The tomb is empty
stories.description: Witness grief turn to hope as the risen Jesus meets Mary and restores his scattered disciples.

introduction.summary: The women discover an empty tomb, the risen Jesus meets grieving and fearful disciples, and resurrection hope sends his followers into the world as witnesses.
introduction.context: Jesus has been crucified and buried before the Sabbath. His followers expect to mourn and care for his body, not to find death overturned.

storySections.title: The Empty Tomb
storySections.content: At dawn on the first day of the week, women go to the tomb with spices. They find the stone moved and the body absent. Heavenly messengers remind them that Jesus had spoken about rising, and the women hurry to tell the disciples.

storySections.title: Mary Hears Her Name
storySections.content: Mary Magdalene remains near the tomb weeping. She sees Jesus but initially assumes he is the gardener. When he speaks her name, recognition replaces grief. Jesus sends her to tell the disciples that she has seen him.

storySections.title: The Road to Emmaus
storySections.content: Two disciples leave Jerusalem discussing the events. Jesus walks with them unrecognised, listens to their disappointment and explains the Scriptures. They recognise him as he breaks bread, then return to share the news.

storySections.title: Peace for Fearful Disciples
storySections.content: Jesus appears among disciples gathered behind locked doors and speaks peace. He shows them his wounds and commissions them. Thomas, absent at first, later encounters Jesus and moves from doubt to a personal confession of faith.

storySections.title: Restored and Sent
storySections.content: By the Sea of Galilee, Jesus meets the disciples after an unsuccessful night of fishing and provides breakfast. He restores Peter through repeated questions of love and entrusts him with care for others. The risen Jesus sends his followers to make disciples among all nations.

flashcards.front: What did they discover?

keyLessons: Resurrection transforms grief without dismissing the reality of loss.
Jesus meets people personally—in tears, questions, fear and failure.
Christian faith is rooted in testimony about the risen Jesus.
Peace is given so that fearful disciples can become courageous witnesses.
Restoration leads to renewed responsibility and service.
The resurrection opens a mission of hope for every nation.

reflection.question: Where do you most need resurrection hope—in grief, doubt, fear or a past failure?
reflection.prompt: Choose one resurrection encounter in this story and write what Jesus gives that person.

stories.prayerPrompt: Risen Jesus, meet me with your peace, restore my hope and send me to live as a faithful witness.
